question.prompt:
The infinite product

\[\sqrt[3]{10}\cdot\sqrt[3]{\sqrt[3]{10}}\cdot\sqrt[3]{\sqrt[3]{\sqrt[3]{10}}}\cdots\]

evaluates to a real number. What is that number?

solutions.title: Add the exponents
solutions.explanation:
Each additional cube root divides the exponent of 10 by 3, so multiplying the factors becomes a geometric-series calculation.

The factors are
\[
10^{1/3},\quad10^{1/9},\quad10^{1/27},\quad\ldots.
\]
Let \(P_N\) be the product of the first \(N\) factors. Multiplication of powers with the same base adds their exponents, giving
\[
P_N=10^{S_N},\qquad
S_N=\frac13+\frac1{3^2}+\cdots+\frac1{3^N}.
\]
This geometric sum has first term \(1/3\) and common ratio \(1/3\), so
\[
S_N=\frac{\frac13(1-3^{-N})}{1-\frac13}
=\frac12(1-3^{-N}).
\]
Because \(3^{-N}\) tends to 0, the exponents tend to \(1/2\). Therefore the infinite product equals
\[
10^{1/2}=\boxed{\sqrt{10}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutions.title: Cube the product
solutions.explanation:
Cubing removes one layer of cube roots from each factor, reproducing the original pattern after an initial factor of 10.

Let \(P_N\) denote the product of the first \(N\) factors. For \(N\ge2\), cubing each factor gives
\[
P_N^3=10P_{N-1}.
\]
Indeed, the first factor becomes 10, and the remaining factors become exactly the first \(N-1\) factors of the original product.

The problem states that these finite products converge to a real number; call it \(L\). Every factor exceeds 1, so
\[
P_N\ge\sqrt[3]{10}>0,
\]
and hence \(L>0\). As \(N\) grows, both \(P_N\) and \(P_{N-1}\) approach \(L\). The finite-product identity therefore gives
\[
L^3=10L.
\]
Dividing by the positive number \(L\), we obtain \(L^2=10\). Taking the positive root yields
\[
L=\boxed{\sqrt{10}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
